title: Extraction of critical metals from chrysotile asbestos tailings  via  an ammonium sulfate roasting-water leaching process
content: Chrysotile asbestos tailings (CATs) are hazardous industrial wastes that contain substantial amounts of valuable critical metals, including Mg, Fe, and Ni. This study investigates the co-extraction of these metals from CATs using an ammonium sulfate ((NH4)2SO4) roasting-water leaching process. Key process parameters, including (NH4)2SO4 dosage, roasting temperature, and roasting time, were systematically optimized to maximize the leaching efficiencies of Mg, Fe, and Ni. The phase transformations and microstructural evolution during roasting were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TG). Under the optimal conditions, the leaching efficiencies of Mg, Fe, and Ni all exceeded 93%. XRD and TG analyses revealed that the roasting process effectively decomposed the chrysotile structure and transformed the metal-bearing phases into water-soluble Fe2(SO4)3, NiSO4, and magnesium sulfate, which were subsequently dissolved during water leaching. The results demonstrate that the proposed process achieves high simultaneous extraction efficiencies for multiple valuable metals while minimizing secondary pollution. This study provides a feasible and cleaner production route for the sustainable utilization of CATs.
